core_obligations: Reduction to the normal form (proof lines 3543-3552): completion preserves Gorenstein, so it suffices to decide when the multicross ring A with n >= 2 branches is Gorenstein.
n = 2 (proof lines 3554-3562): A = k[[x, y]]/(xy) is a complete intersection, hence Gorenstein by the lci lemma applied to the regular (Gorenstein) ring k[[x, y]].

n > 2 (proof lines 3564-3582): if A were Gorenstein then R Hom(k, A) = k[n] for some n, forcing Ext^1_A(k, A) to be k or 0; but the sequence 0 -> m_A -> A -> k -> 0 gives Ext^1_A(k, A) = Hom_A(m_A, A)/A, and the n - 1 coordinate functionals e_i are k-linearly independent in the quotient, so dim_k Ext^1_A(k, A) >= n - 1 >= 2, a contradiction.
proof_roadmap: Transfer Gorenstein to the completed multicross normal form via flat unramified completion.
Verify the node case n = 2 as a complete intersection.
For n > 2 derive the Gorenstein constraint on Ext^1 and compute Hom_A(m_A, A)/A with the coordinate functionals.
Conclude the dimension lower bound contradicting the Gorenstein constraint.
difficulty_reason: The lemma classifies Gorenstein multicross singularities as nodes (statement lines 3535-3541). The proof (lines 3543-3582) reduces to the completed normal form, settles n = 2 by the complete-intersection criterion, and for n > 2 runs a homological algebra computation: the Gorenstein constraint R Hom(k, A) = k[n], the long exact sequence giving Ext^1_A(k, A) = Hom_A(m_A, A)/A, and n - 1 independent coordinate functionals forcing dim >= 2. The linear independence of the e_i is a small inline check flagged to the reader; the load-bearing computation is present. H2: one coherent homological computation with a clean contradiction.
